div.head: Ger 19
div.ab: Ic gecende be ðam ðe ic cuðe; se ðe bet cunne, gecyðe his mare.
ic ge|cende be ðam ðe ic cuðe . se ðe bet cunne ge|cyðe his mare
Ic gecende be ðam ðe ic cuðe; se ðe bet cunne, gecyðe his mare.
Ich habe erklärt gemäss dem, was ich konnte [kannte]; wer besser kann [kennt], künde dessen mehr!
I have set out what I could [knew]; let him who can [knows] better make more of it known!
I have spoken about that which I know; he who knows better should make known more.
I have revealed what I know; let anyone who knows better make known more.
div.note: 2 and 19. ‘hyrdas folces’ is what Polity 12 calls the reeves. K: ‘holden’ corrected to ‘holdan’; spacing corrected. In another 12th-century hand there follows a list of ship-levies from the estates of the London church c. 1000. Liebermann compares Rect 21.1.
